meta.titre: Simple past for a single completed action

sections.contenu_markdown: Some verbs describe an instant, not a duration: they almost always take the simple past, never the past continuous.

The simple past is used for a single completed action at a specific past moment; 'notice' describes an instantaneous perception, not a prolonged or repeated action, so it takes the simple past ('did you notice') rather than the past continuous.

sections.enonce_markdown: Complete: 'When you passed the town hall clock, ___ what time it was?'

etapes.action: Analyse the nature of the verb 'notice'
etapes.justification: Noticing something happens at a single instant, not over a duration.
Instantaneous actions take the simple past, not the past continuous.

sections.conclusion_markdown: "When you passed the town hall clock, did you notice what time it was?"

items.erreur_markdown: Using the past continuous ('were you noticing') because the sentence also contains 'passed', which might suggest a background action.
items.pourquoi_faux: The past continuous ('passed... while noticing') would only work if 'noticing' described an ongoing process interrupted by another action; but noticing the time is instantaneous, not prolonged.
items.correction_markdown: Ask whether the verb describes a process with duration (past continuous possible) or an instant perception (simple past required).

items.enonce_markdown: Choose the correct form: 'I (was reading / read) a book when the phone rang.'
items.solution_markdown: was reading (an ongoing background action interrupted by a punctual event, 'the phone rang', in the simple past).

items_markdown: Instantaneous verbs (notice, realise, recognise) usually take the simple past
Past continuous suits ongoing background actions, often interrupted by a simple past event
